picks.title: Jacobs, Maloy, Beyer Release Outline For Sweeping, Bipartisan AI Safety Legislation
picks.source: Office of Rep. Sara Jacobs (U.S. House)
picks.rationale: Primary document: bipartisan SAFE AI Act outline would mandate safety frameworks, incident reporting and transparency for frontier labs, which is a new federal bill on the policy axis.
picks.excerpt: Reps. Jacobs (D-CA), Maloy (R-UT) and Beyer (D-VA) released an outline of the bipartisan SAFE AI Act, forthcoming legislation that would mandate safety frameworks, incident reporting and transparency from frontier AI labs under federal oversight.

picks.title: Trump administration approved more than 879,000 AI chip sales to Chinese companies, per new disclosure.
picks.rationale: Geopolitics axis: newly released Commerce Department license data (via House Foreign Affairs Chair Mast) quantifies approved AI-chip sales to China, ahead of Jensen Huang's testimony.
picks.excerpt: House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast released Commerce Department license data showing more than 879,000 advanced AI chips approved for sale to Chinese companies (of ~3.4M requested), ahead of Jensen Huang's testimony; Ranking Member Meeks says licenses were approved with little scrutiny.

picks.title: Governor Newsom's nation-leading AI safety framework is getting even stronger as California releases next steps on mandatory safety standards and oversight
picks.source: Office of the Governor of California
picks.rationale: State-level primary release: recommendations for mandatory frontier-AI standards, independent oversight and emergency shutdown authority on top of SB 53.
picks.excerpt: California released expert recommendations for mandatory frontier-AI safety standards, independent oversight, emergency shutdown ('kill switch') authority for dangerous systems and limits on self-improving AI, as next steps on top of SB 53.

picks.title: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert
picks.rationale: Liability litigation: a new lawsuit over a public-sector AI surveillance deployment, alleging that more than 99% of the system's alerts were false positives.
picks.excerpt: Four Baltimore County students sued their school system and police after an AI gun-detection system flagged a Doritos bag as a weapon; the suit alleges over 99% of the system's alerts were false positives.

picks.title: Don't buy smart glasses, Dutch data watchdog advises
picks.rationale: Regulator action in Europe: the Dutch DPA formally advises consumers against AI smart glasses, citing safety failures in tests and privacy risks to bystanders.
picks.excerpt: The Dutch data protection authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens) advised consumers not to buy AI smart glasses, citing tests where devices misread medicine instructions or pretended to call an ambulance, plus privacy risks to bystanders.
